calls.reason: The Kadrey ruling confirms Meta downloaded LibGen and trained on it, but no evidence verifies Marcus's search results or counts more than 100 of his works among what Meta acquired.

A Dec 2023 internal memo, as quoted in a publishers' complaint, calls LibGen a dataset Meta knew to be pirated. The June 2025 Kadrey ruling found Meta added the downloaded books to Llama training data anyway.
In its March 2025 answer, Meta admits LibGen data was used to train Llama 3. The court's January 2025 order quotes an employee calling LibGen a dataset Meta knew to be pirated.
No work-by-work training records or permission records exist for Marcus's works. The Authors Guild notes it is unclear whether Meta used every LibGen book, so 'every single case' cannot be checked.

An internal document says the LibGen decision came after an escalation to MZ, but Zuckerberg testified he had no knowledge of LibGen and no involvement in its use. The evidence on personal sign-off is mixed.
